appointment_prerequisites: Best-interest finding for the appointment itself
subdivision_a_consideration_bar.standards_compliance: Evaluation must comply with Judicial Council standards under § 3117 (rule 5.220 methodology; rule 5.225 qualifications)
subdivision_a_consideration_bar.filing_rule: Written confidential report filed with the clerk
subdivision_a_consideration_bar.service_rule: Served on parties / attorneys / § 3150 minor's counsel at least 10 days before the custody hearing
subdivision_a_consideration_bar.consideration_bar: 'May be considered by the court only if' conducted in compliance with § 3117 standards. Nonsubstantive/inconsequential errors do not preclude consideration; substantive defects do.

subdivision_b_confidentiality.doctrinal_note: Closed list. Any other disclosure is unwarranted under subdivision (f).

subdivision_c_stipulated_admission.rule: Report may be received in evidence on stipulation of all interested parties; competent evidence as to all matters contained.
subdivision_c_stipulated_admission.doctrinal_note: Without stipulation, § 3111 itself does not establish admissibility; Evid. § 720 foundation remains a separate gate.

subdivision_d_sanctions.amount: Sufficient to deter repetition; may include attorney fees and costs

verbatim_factor_inventory.subdivision_e_mandatory_form: Judicial Council form informing recipient of confidentiality and consequences of unwarranted disclosure must be served with every court-ordered evaluation report (rule of court required by January 1, 2010)

elements: Not in the best interest of the child

steward_case_relevance_audit.purpose: Map § 3111 against every custody evaluator, evaluator-equivalent, or § 730/§ 3118 appointee in the steward's case file. For each appointment, ask: (1) was the appointment supported by a best-interest finding? (2) did the evaluation comply with rule 5.220 methodology and rule 5.225 qualifications? (3) was the report filed with the clerk and served 10 days before hearing? (4) was the § 3111(e) confidentiality form served with the report? (5) was dissemination limited to the statutory channels? Any 'no' is a consideration-bar defect.

factor_audits.audit_recommendation: For each evaluator of record, verify rule 5.225 credentialing compliance: primary license state, California license status, continuing-education declarations, qualification on the specific clinical or forensic subject matter addressed in the report. NPPES cross-check is operationally decisive for out-of-jurisdiction appointments.
factor_audits.audit_status: CRITICAL — ties directly to FAMLAW-006 F-006-01 Wiita NPPES finding (primary license SC; CA practice footprint LAC; appointment in Contra Costa).

factor_audits.audit_recommendation: For each evaluator report of record, verify (i) 10-day service, (ii) § 3111(e) confidentiality form served with the report, (iii) dissemination limited to statutory channels. Any procedural defect independently bars consideration.
If the record reflects no stipulation by all interested parties, then § 3111(c) did not authorize admission. Admission without foundation under Evid. § 720 is an independent error.
For any § 3044 perpetration finding rested on an evaluator's conclusion, § 3044(e) independently prohibits the finding. § 3111 compliance does not cure § 3044(e) non-compliance.
factor_audits.audit_status: CRITICAL — pairs with FAMLAW-004 (§ 3044 never rebutted).

factor_audits.audit_recommendation: If any evaluation was conducted remotely across county or state lines, Bus. & Prof. § 2290.5 telehealth-scope rules apply on top of § 3111. Record the modality of each evaluation session.
